Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are out in the middle. Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie are the two openers for Ireland. Trent Boult has been given the new ball and is raring to go. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, New Zealand have the bowling firepower to defend this total but they need to be wary of the threat that Ireland possess with the bat. If the Irish team survives the initial burst with the new ball from the Kiwis, we will be in for a riveting chase. Stay tuned...

The hat-trick hero Josh Little comes up for a quick chat. Says that there was a bit of tail on offer at the backend and he tried to bring the ball into the batters and hoped that they miss it. Admits that they should have bowled fuller earlier when the swing was on offer. Feels that there is no reason why they cannot get the target and cause another upset.

All the talk around Kane Williamson's form and approach in this format was put to bed. He smashed a 35-ball 61 to propel New Zealand in the end overs but his departure forced a mini-collapse. Josh Little claimed a hat-trick, the second of this edition, and his efforts were the prime reason that the Kiwis didn't get the desired finish.

New Zealand looked slightly scratchy at the start but slowly grew into the Powerplay overs, all thanks to Finn Allen's blitz with the bat. Devon Conway was dropped on one by Harry Tector but his innings never got going and he got eventually dismissed after his participation in a slow partnership with Kane Williamson. Glenn Phillips' arrival injected some momentum into New Zealand's innings and although his stay was short, he did the job of setting the tone.

Incredible piece of bowling in the last two overs from Ireland and that stopped New Zealand from touching the 200-run mark. The Irish team will be feeling the momentum behind them after finishing on a hight but they still have a big target in front to overhaul.
A couple of runs to end the innings! Mark Adair bowls another low full toss, on off, Daryl Mitchell mistimes his drive down to long off for a couple of runs. New Zealand finish on 185 for 6!
Short of a length and on off, slower too, Daryl Mitchell punches it past extra cover for a brace.
A full toss and on off, Daryl Mitchell slaps it towards the bowler where Mark Adair gets a hand to it and parries it towards long on. Two runs taken!
This is another brilliant yorker, outside off, Daryl Mitchell moves across to play at it but cannot connect.
Mark Adair nails the yorker, on off, Tim Southee tries to dig it out, but misses and it goes through the keeper. The batter gets a bye.
WIDE! Mark Adair bangs in a bouncer, on middle, Tim Southee ducks under it. It is called a wide for height.
Mark Adair bowls a full toss on outside off, Daryl Mitchell smashes it to the right of cover where the fielder does well to stop it diving to that side. A single is taken.
Mark Adair to bowl the last over.
Slower length ball on middle, Daryl Mitchell turns it in the gap on the leg side, through square leg, for a single. What an over - a hat-trick in it and just three runs.
A length ball around off, Tim Southee walks forward and taps it down to the off side for a run.
Tim Southee is in next.

OUT! PLUMB IN FRONT! HAT-TRICK FOR LITTLE! Josh Little fires in a good length delivery, on middle, skidding through, Mitchell Santner is very late to put his bat down to play at it and gets rapped around his pads right in front of the stumps. There is a huge appeal for LBW, and up goes the finger. The Irish players are delighted. However, Mitchell Santner takes the review. UltraEdge shows no bat involved and Ball Tracking shows three reds. The hat-trick stands, the second of this edition after Karthik Meiyappan's against Sri Lanka.
Mitchell Santner is ready to face the hat-trick ball.

OUT! GIVEN LBW! James Neesham has decided to review the decision. Looks out to the naked eye. Coming to the delivery, it's a bit on the shorter side, around middle and angling in, James Neesham hangs back to heave it over the leg side but it stays low and strikes him on the back leg. The appeal is made and the finger goes up. DRS time! The UltraEdge shows nothing and the Ball Tracking confirms three reds. A golden duck for Neesham and Little is on a hat-trick.
James Neesham arrives with 10 balls remaining in the innings. He has the license to unleash.

OUT! TAKEN! Josh Little gets the big wicket of Kane Williamson who was looking dangerous. Little bangs this short and on middle, Kane Williamson goes for the pull shot, but hits it with the top half of his bat and fails to get the required power. As a result, the ball flies in the air and towards deep square leg where Gareth Delany takes a nice catch moving to his right.
Commentary.Howout: c Gareth Delany b Josh Little

Commentary.Commentary: On a length and on middle, Daryl Mitchell nudges it through square leg for a single.
Josh Little to bowl the penultimate over.

SIX! BANG! Kane Williamson clears the fence! Barry McCarthy serves this full and on middle, Kane Williamson stays there and heaves it over the deep mid-wicket fence for another maximum. 21 from the over and New Zealand are finishing on a high.
FOUR! Slashed away! This is short and outside off with third man up in the circle, Kane Williamson slices it over short third man for a boundary.

SIX! FIFTY FOR KANE! Barry McCarthy bowls this full and on middle, Kane Williamson goes down and slog-sweeps it over the deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie. This has been a good knock from him and he will look to take New Zealand to a good total now.
Back of a length and outside off, Daryl Mitchell cuts it towards sweeper cover for a single.
Dropped! A full toss around leg, Daryl Mitchell flicks it uppishly towards short fine leg where Josh Little spills it out. Two runs taken!
Barry McCarthy tries to go for the yorker, but bowls a low full toss, on off, Daryl Mitchell drives it wide of long on for two runs.
Barry McCarthy to bowl out.
Mark Adair serves this full and around leg, Kane Williamson flicks it through mid-wicket for a brace.
A good yorker now, outside off, Daryl Mitchell moves across a bit and digs it towards point for one.
This is pitched up, on middle, Daryl Mitchell lofts it towards long on for a couple of runs.
FOUR! Nice shot! Mark Adair changes his pace again and bowls this short of a length, on off, Daryl Mitchell stays there and smashes it over cover for a boundary.
Mark Adair lands this short and on middle, Kane Williamson pulls it towards deep square leg for a run.
This is full and outside off, Daryl Mitchell drills it down to long off for a single.
Wide! Mark Adair goes for the slower one, but loses his line and bowls this well outside off, Daryl Mitchell leaves it alone. It is called a wide.
Mark Adair is back on. 1 for 19 in his 2 overs so far.
Floated, full and on off, Kane Williamson drives it through cover for a couple of runs. 12 runs from the over!
FOUR! Poor delivery and rightly punished! This is short and on middle, Kane Williamson picks up the length early, goes back and pulls it wide of deep mid-wicket for a boundary.
Tossed up, full and on off, Kane Williamson goes inside-out and chips it towards deep extra cover for a brace.
Shortish and on middle, Kane Williamson goes on his back foot and slaps it down the ground but it hits Daryl Mitchell and goes nowhere.
FOUR! Kane Williamson finds the gap this time! George Dockrell bowls this quicker, full and on leg, Kane Williamson goes down and sweeps it towards the deep backward square leg fence for a boundary.
Short and on leg, Kane Williamson moves back and pulls it straight to mid-wicket.
George Dockrell comes back into the attack.

FOUR! Put away with ease. Josh Little bowls a slower one again, a bit short and around leg at 107 kph, Daryl Mitchell shuffles across, picks the change in pace and pulls it with excellent timing to deep square leg. Finds the gap and boundary.
Wide! This time the line is way too wide outside off, Daryl Mitchell leaves it alone.
Around middle, again short in length, Williamson gets back and pulls it to deep square leg for a single.

Uppish but safe! Slower one again, a touch on the shorter side around off at 110 kph, Daryl Mitchell punches it uppishly towards mid off but it doesn't carry to the fielder. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end and they cross for an overthrow.
Goes slow and short outside off, Kane waits and pulls it to deep mid-wicket. Another single.
A length delivery around middle, Daryl Mitchell tucks it to square leg for a run.
Back of a length, around off, Kane pulls it to deep mid-wicket for one.
Josh Little (2-0-9-0) comes back into the attack now.
Drops it short and on middle, Kane hangs back and pulls it to deep mid-wicket for a single. 4-0-30-2, a good effort from the leggie.
Fuller and on middle, flicked through mid-wicket for one.
Flatter and on middle, Mitchell tries to flick but fails to get the connection right. It rolls ont he leg side.
Quicker around off, Daryl Mitchell shuffles across and spoons it wide of short fine leg for two runs.
Fuller and around middle, Daryl plays the reverse sweep but finds point.
Daryl Mitchell comes out to the middle now.

OUT! Phillips holes out and this is a massive breakthrough for the Irish team. Gareth Delany shows the courage to toss it up and smartly keeps the line outside off again. Glenn Phillips reaches out for it and tries to smash it over extra cover but fails to get the desired connection. It flies towards sweeper cover where George Dockrell takes a fantastic sliding catch. A short and breezy stay for Glenn is over.
Commentary.Howout: c George Dockrell b Gareth Delany

Commentary.Commentary: Barry goes fuller and on middle, Glenn knocks it down to long on and retains strike with a single. 39 runs for New Zealand after the Drinks break.

FOUR! Power again, placement again! This is superb batting. Back of a length, around off and angling in, Glenn Phillips rocks back and pulls it powerfully across the line. He finds the gap at wide long on for his second boundary in the over.
FOUR! Power and placement from Glenn! Short again, in the channel outside off, Phillips latches onto the width and hammers it over covers for a boundary.
Shortish and on off, Glenn Phillips stays on the back foot and plays it down to point.
A length ball on off, Kane helps it in the vacant area at mid-wicket for a single.
Fuller in length and outside off, Phillips opens the face and drives it through cover-point for a single.
Barry McCarthy (2-0-14-0) is back on.
Loopy and full, around off, Williamson leans forward and wrists it to mid-wicket. A dot ball to end an eventful over.
Shortish and around leg, punched down to long on for a single.

SIX! Boom! Glenn Phillips opens his account in a grand fashion. Fuller and quicker, around leg, Glenn kneels down and smokes it over mid-wicket for a biggie. He is the batter in form and this shot will get him going.
Flatter and shorter, around off, Glenn defends it back from the crease.
Glenn Phillips walks out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Smart bowling from Gareth Delany. He serves a googly and keeps the line outside off. Devon Conway goes down for the slog sweep but has to drag it from quite wide. Ends up getting it away from the bottom half of his bat and the ball flies straight into the hands of Mark Adair at long on. Conway's unconvincing stay in the middle comes to an end. This could be a blessing in disguise for the Black Caps.
Commentary.Howout: c Mark Adair b Gareth Delany

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and wide outside off, Conway throws his hands at it and slices it behind short third man for a couple of runs.
Wide! Fires a flat delivery way wide outside off, Conway leaves it alone.
Gareth Delany comes back for his third over. He has conceded 17 runs in his first two overs.

SIX! High and handsome! Kane Williamson has decided to switch gears now. Fionn goes short and around middle, Williamson gets on top of the bounce, swivels on the back foot and pulls it all the way over deep square leg for a biggie. 18 from the over!

FOUR! Wonderful shot from Kane! New Zealand will hope that this shot will get him going. Full in length and around middle, Williamson skips down the track and lofts it with a straight bat, behind the bowler and finds the second boundary of this over.
Steps down the track and has to reach out for a delivery wide outside off. Conway gets some connection and sends it to sweeper cover for a single.

FOUR! A much-needed boundary for the Black Caps and Devon Conway. Short in length, around off, Conway rocks back and pulls it from the middle of the bat. It races in front of square on the leg side and finds the gap.
Slower one, full and around off, Devon Conway backs away a bit and then plays a mistimed lofted shot off the inner half. It drops towards mid on and they get two runs.
A bit short and around off, angling in, Kane stays back and runs it down to third man for a single.

Drinks break. New Zealand started slowly but then picked pace in the Powerplay, all thanks to Finn Allen, again. He played some excellent shots to up the run rate but got dismissed in the sixth over. Devon Conway, who was dropped on 1, has found it tough to play his natural free-flowing game so far and currently, he is amidst a slow partnership with Kane Williamson. Ireland will be pleased with their work and would like to keep a strong hand on the scoring rate in the middle overs. Let's see how the next phase unfurls. Fionn Hand to bowl after the break...
Short again, on middle and leg, Kane Williamson nudges it towards deep mid-wicket for one more.
Shortish and around off, Devon Conway moves back and cuts it through cover-point for a single.
WIDE! George Dockrell tries to use the angle, but bowls this too far outside off, Devon Conway leaves it alone. Wided.
Quicker again and outside off, angling away too, Devon Conway mistimes his attempted lofted drive back to the bowler.
Shorter in length and on middle, Kane Williamson forces it wide of long on for a run.
Floated, full and on off, Devon Conway slog-sweeps it towards deep mid-wicket for just a single.
WIDE! George Dockrell bowls this flatter and outside off, way outside off. Wided.
George Dockrell starts with a quicker delivery, outside off, angling away, Devon Conway lets it go to the keeper.
George Dockrell is introduced into the attack.

Good work in the deep! This is served on a back of a length and outside off, Kane Williamson cuts through backward point and it races away. Curtis Campher covers his ground well from third man and dives to his right to parry it to the fielder coming across from sweeper cover. Two runs are taken!
A slower one now, on a length and on off, Devon Conway guides it through backward point for another run.
Barry McCarthy bowls this on a good length and around off, Kane Williamson punches it off the back foot towards sweeper cover for one.
This is on a yorker length and on middle, Devon Conway squeezes it out towards mid off for a run.
Fuller again and on middle, Kane Williamson clips it towards deep mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Up and over! Barry McCarthy serves this full and around off, Kane Williamson stays in his crease and chips it over covers for a boundary.
Barry McCarthy comes back into the attack for his second over.
Slower through the air, on off, Devon Conway decides to go for the sweep but changes his mind at the last moment and guides it towards short third man.
Flatter and quicker, on middle and leg, Kane Williamson tucks it through mid-wicket for another one.

Floated, full and outside off, Devon Conway skips down the track, trying to go inside-out over extra cover but ends up hitting it a bit too straight. The ball hurries down to long off and only a single results.
Shortish again and on middle, Kane Williamson flicks it off the back foot through square leg for a single.
A bit short and on middle, Kane Williamson moves back and knocks it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up, full and on leg, Kane Williamson goes for the sweep but misses and gets hit on the pads.
Andy Balbirnie keeps on ringing the changes. Gareth Delany is back on. His first over went for 13 runs and in a way handed the momentum to New Zealand. Can he redeem himself?
Fionn Hand bowls this on a yorker length and on middle, Kane Williamson takes a couple of steps down the pitch and digs it towards mid on for a quick run.
This is pitched up, on off, Devon Conway drills it towards long off for a single.
A slower one now, on a length and on off, Devon Conway skips down the track but only manages to push it to cover.
On a length and around middle, Kane Williamson knocks it wide of mid on for a single and gets off the mark.
Full again and on middle, shaping in a bit, Kane Williamson works it towards mid on.
Fionn Hand starts with a full delivery, on off, Devon Conway drives it towards deep point for a single.
Change in bowling. The field restriction is lifted and here comes Fionn Hand.
BEATEN! Mark Adair bowls this on a good length and around the fifth stump line, angling in, Kane Williamson looks to play at it but gets beaten. At the end of the Powerplay, New Zealand are 52 for 1.
Kane Williamson is in next, at number 3.

OUT! TAKEN! Finn Allen tries to play another attacking shot, but is dismissed this time. Mark Adair gets the much-needed breakthrough for Ireland. He bowls this fuller and around off, Finn Allen tries to go over mid off but smashes it flat and straight into the hands of Fionn Hand who takes a sharp catch near his chest. There was very little reaction time for the fielder as the ball was travelling. New Zealand lose their first as Finn walks back dejected.
Commentary.Howout: c Fionn Hand b Mark Adair

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Another boundary for Allen! This is the back-of-the-hand slower one, full and on middle, Finn Allen reads it well, stays there and lofts it over the bowler's head for four more runs.
SIX! BANG! Great shot! Mark Adair bowls this short again and on middle, Finn Allen moves across a bit and hooks it over the fine leg fence for a biggie.
WIDE! Mark Adair tries the slower one, but bowls it full and outside off, Finn Allen uses his feet and tries to reach for it but misses. It is called a wide.
This is full and outside off, Devon Conway drives it through cover-point for a single.
FOUR! Devon Conway finally finds the fence! Mark Adair lands this short and around leg, Devon Conway stays there and pulls it towards the deep square leg fence for a boundary.
Mark Adair is back on.

FOUR! Stand and deliver! A 143 kph delivery, full and outside off, right in the slot for the batter. Finn Allen attacks it with all his power and pumps it over mid off for a boundary. A good over is spoiled.
Fuller in length on middle, angling down at 139 kph, Conway tries to whip it across the line but misses. It deflects off his pads to square leg and they gather another leg bye.

Change in pace. Slightly short and around off, angling away at 125 kph, Finn shuffles across to heave it over the leg side but is early into his shot. It takes the thigh pad and goes towards cover-point. They cross for a leg bye.
Back of a length, around middle and leg, trying to follow the batter. Conway pushes it gently to mid off and scampers across to the other end.
Little keeps it around off, on a length, Conway defends it from the inner portion of his blade.
Fractionally short and on off, Conway taps it down to backward point and looks for a run. His partner sends him back as the ball is too close to the fielder.
Josh Little comes back into the attack. He conceded 4 runs in his first over.
Quicker and shorter on off, it's punched to extra cover. 13 from the over!
FOUR! Finn is cashing in against some loose bowling. Short again from Gareth Delany, around leg, Finn hangs deep inside the crease and slaps it over extra cover for yet another boundary.
FOUR! Finn is getting into the act now. Shortish and around leg, once again Finn makes room as he jumps down the track and forces it down the ground towards long on for a boundary.
Flatter and shorter, around leg, Finn goes back to cut but mistimes it towards cover-point.
FOUR! Aerial but in the gap! Loopy delivery, full and around leg, Finn Allen makes room for himself and drills it aerially past mid off for a boundary.
Starts with a flighted delivery, landing full on off, Conway flicks it through mid-wicket and rotates the strike.
Ireland going with spin now as Gareth Delany comes into the attack.
Mishit! A length ball outside off, Finn steps back and throws his bat at it. It comes off from the toe end of the bat and flies towards mid off. The ball drops safely and they get two runs.
Back of a length, around leg, Conway attempts to glance but misses. It goes off his thigh pad to backward point. They cross for a leg bye.
Another play and a miss. In the channel outside off, on a length, Conway reaches out, trying to cut, but misses.
On a good length and around off, Conway advances down the track and tries to slap it through the line but misses.
Too full in length and around off, 139 kph, Finn drags his attempted shot and sends it through mid-wicket off the inner edge. They get a run.
Run out chance missed! Fullish and around off, Conway bunts it towards mid off and goes for a quick run. The fielder misses his shy at the bowler's end otherwise Conway would have been a goner.
Barry McCarthy replaces Josh Little.
Adair goes short and around middle, shaping in, Allen tries to pull but makes no connection. Two good overs from Ireland.

PUT DOWN! Early life for Conway. Fuller and around off, Devon Conway runs down the track to smack it through the line. It goes aerially to Harry Tector at mid off who tries to catch it over his head but it bursts out of his hands. They get three runs. The replay shows that the ball was travelling and took off while reaching the fielder. Can't be an excuse though, that should have been taken at this level.
Around leg, on a length, Conway fails to put it away and wears it on his pads.
Finds the fielder. Adair pitches it up and outside off, Conway plays a flowing drive off the front foot but finds the fielder at cover-point. A slight fumble but no run is taken.
Better from Adair this time. He serves it on a length around middle, getting it to angle away from the batter, Conway covers the line and makes a leave.
Four leg byes! Poor line from Adair. Begins with a full ball down the leg side, 83 mph, Conway misses the flick but it tickles his pads and runs wide of the keeper. A boundary results at fine leg.
Mark Adair to share the new ball.
A touch short and on off, Allen sits back to heave it over the leg side. But it takes the inner half and rolls away from short fine leg. They get two runs.
Swing and a miss! This is how Finn bats. Josh Little gets this one to angle away from the right-hander, on a good length and outside off, Allen tries to power it through the line but misses.
Lands it on a length this time, outside off, Allen shows his fast hands as he smashes it through the line. Again finds the fielder at cover-point.
Shortish and on off, Allen goes on the back foot and punches. He finds the fielder at cover-point. Not much movement so far.
Little is yet to get his line right. He drifts on the pads, fuller in length, Devon Conway clips it through square leg and picks up a single.
Back of a length, around middle, Finn Allen turns and pulls it behind square leg. The fielder stops it in the deep and they cross for a single.

We are ready for some action now! The Irish players are taking their respective field positions. Finn Allen and Devon Conway are the two openers for New Zealand. Josh Little to start proceedings with the ball. Let's play...
The umpires and the players have lined up in the middle for the national anthems. It will be New Zealand's national anthem first followed by the national anthem of Ireland.

Kane Williamson, the captain of New Zealand, says that it's a good surface and they will try to assess the conditions in order to get a good score on the board. Tells that they have got their lessons from the last game and have picked out the positives. Mentions that Ireland are a strong side and they want to focus on their plans and execution. Kane informs that New Zealand are also unchanged.

Andy Balbirnie, the Irish captain, says that they want to bowl first as the pitch should play well for 40 overs. Wants his team to give one big push and see where they stand after the match. Informs that they have opted for the same XI.

New Zealand (Unchanged Playing XI) - Finn Allen, Devon Conway (WK), Kane Williamson (C), Glenn Phillips, James Neesham, Daryl Mitchell, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson, Trent Boult.

Ireland (Unchanged Playing XI) - Paul Stirling, Andy Balbirnie (C), Lorcan Tucker (WK), Harry Tector, Curtis Campher, George Dockrell, Gareth Delany, Mark Adair, Fionn Hand, Barry McCarthy, Josh Little.
TOSS - Ireland have won the toss and they have elected to BOWL first.
Pitch report - A fresh pitch is to be used. The square boundaries are on the shorter side. Michael Atherton informs that it's a drop-in pitch, firm, nicely grassed and runs to be had.

Ireland, on the other hand, can be called the giant killer in this World Cup. They took down the Windies in the Group Stages and then got the better of England in the Super 12s. They have a well-rounded team, and they will be looking to cause another upset and spoil the party for the Kiwis. Will they be able to do so? Or will the Black Caps get the victory? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

New Zealand have been the top performer in this group except for their defeat against England. They have managed to find different match-winners, and that is why they are in a solid position to get to the next stage. The Kiwis just need to focus on getting a win here, and they will become the first team to qualify for the semi-finals due to their better NRR than all the other teams.

Hello and a warm welcome, folks! It is time for Match 25 in the Super 12 stage of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022, where Ireland will be locking horns against New Zealand. We can expect an exciting clash as the Kiwis eye progression to the next round while the Irish play for their pride.
... MATCH DAY ...
